description: Use this to identify which Zernio account is connected, for example when the user has several Zernio accounts or asks who they are signed in as. Returns the stable account id plus name and email when available. Do not use it to look up other people.
name: get_profile

id.description: Stable Zernio user id for the signed-in account
id.title: Id

title: Get signed-in Zernio profile

description: Use this when the user wants to see which social media accounts are connected to Zernio, or before scheduling or publishing so you can pass the right account_ids. Returns each account's id, platform, username and connection status. Optionally filter by platform (instagram, tiktok, youtube, twitter, linkedin, facebook, threads, pinterest, reddit, bluesky, googlebusiness, telegram, snapchat, discord, slack).

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous page. Keep the same platform.

platform.description: Only return accounts on this platform

name: list_social_accounts

id.description: Account id to pass as account_id / account_ids
id.title: Id

title: List connected social accounts

description: Use this when the user wants to review their scheduled, draft, published or failed posts, for example 'what is scheduled this week' or 'which posts failed'. Returns each post's id, status, text, scheduled time and per-platform status. Newest first. For one post's full details use get_post; for performance numbers use get_post_analytics.

account_id.description: Only posts targeting this social account

name: list_posts

status.description: draft, scheduled, publishing, published, failed or partial
status.title: Status

title: List posts

description: Use this when the user asks about one specific post: its full text, media, schedule, per-platform status, public links or failure reason. Requires the post id from list_posts or from an earlier create result.
name: get_post

status.description: draft, scheduled, publishing, published, failed or partial
status.title: Status

title: Get post details

description: Use this whenever the user asks whether a text or media can go out, fits, or is allowed on a chosen platform, for example character limits or required media, and before scheduling when in doubt. Use it instead of answering from general knowledge: the rules are enforced by Zernio. Nothing is created. Returns valid true/false plus each error or warning with the platform it applies to.

account_ids.description: Target social account ids from list_social_accounts

media_urls.description: Public image, video or PDF URLs to attach

name: validate_post
title: Check a post against platform rules

description: Use this when the user wants a post published later at a specific time on one or more of their connected accounts. The post stays editable and cancellable until that time. Requires the text, the account_ids from list_social_accounts and the time. Media is attached from public URLs. For publishing right now use publish_post_now instead; for a text-only check use validate_post.

account_ids.description: Target social account ids from list_social_accounts

content.description: Post text. Platform limits apply, for example 280 characters on X

media_urls.description: Public image, video or PDF URLs to attach

scheduled_for.description: When to publish, ISO 8601 such as 2026-10-01T09:00:00+02:00

timezone.description: IANA timezone, needed only when scheduled_for has no UTC offset

name: schedule_post

status.description: draft, scheduled, publishing, published, failed or partial
status.title: Status

title: Schedule a post

description: Use this only when the user explicitly wants the post live right now on one or more of their connected accounts. The content becomes public on those platforms immediately and this cannot be undone from ChatGPT, so confirm the final text and accounts with the user first. Calling it twice publishes twice. Returns the post with its public links. To publish later use schedule_post.

account_ids.description: Target social account ids from list_social_accounts

content.description: Post text. Platform limits apply, for example 280 characters on X

media_urls.description: Public image, video or PDF URLs to attach

status.title: Status

title: Publish a post immediately

description: Use this when the user wants to change the text, media, title or publish time of a post that has not been published yet (draft, scheduled or failed). Only the fields given are changed; new media_urls replace the existing media. Published posts cannot be edited here. Requires the post id from list_posts.

media_urls.description: Replacement media URLs; an empty list removes media

timezone.description: IANA timezone, needed only when scheduled_for has no UTC offset

title.description: New title for YouTube or Pinterest

description: Use this when the user wants to delete a draft, scheduled or failed post so it will not be published. This removes the post from Zernio and cannot be undone. Posts that are already published are left untouched and this tool reports that. Requires the post id from list_posts.
name: cancel_scheduled_post
title: Cancel a scheduled post

description: Use this when a post shows status failed and the user wants Zernio to try publishing it again on the platforms that failed. This publishes the same content publicly on retry, so confirm with the user first. Requires the post id from list_posts. Read the failure reason with get_post before retrying; a reconnect or content fix may be needed first.

post_id.description: Zernio post id of a failed post

name: retry_failed_post

status.title: Status

title: Retry a failed post

description: Use this when the user asks how a specific published post performed: impressions, reach, likes, comments, shares, saves, clicks, views and engagement rate, per platform. Numbers sync from the platforms periodically, so a just-published post may report pending data. Requires the post id from list_posts.

post_id.description: Zernio post id of a published post

name: get_post_analytics
title: Get analytics for one post

description: Use this when the user asks how their accounts or platforms performed over a period, for example 'how did Instagram do last month'. Returns daily totals (impressions, reach, likes, comments, shares, saves, clicks, views) and per-platform totals for the date range, defaulting to the last 30 days. Filter by account_id or platform. For a single post use get_post_analytics.

from_date.description: Start date YYYY-MM-DD, default 30 days ago

platform.description: Only this platform, for example instagram

name: get_account_analytics
title: Get daily analytics across accounts

description: Use this when the user asks when they should post for the most engagement. Computed from the engagement history of the user's own published posts, as weekday and hour in UTC, best first. Filter by account_id or platform. Returns nothing useful until the account has published posts with synced analytics.

platform.description: Only this platform, for example instagram
